verses.text: When Jabin king of Hazor heard about this, he sent messages to Jobab king of Madon, and to the kings of Shimron and Akshaph,
and to the kings in the northern hill country, in the Jordan valley south of the Sea of Galilee, in the western foothills, and in the hills of Dor to the west.
He also sent to the Canaanites in the east and the west, to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites and Jebusites in the hill country, and to the Hivites below Mount Hermon in the region of Mizpah.
They came out with all their armies, a huge crowd of soldiers, as many as the grains of sand on the seashore, with a great many horses and chariots.
All these kings joined together and camped at the Waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. By this time tomorrow I will hand all of them over to Israel, dead. You must cut the leg muscles of their horses and burn their chariots."
So Joshua and his whole army came against them suddenly at the Waters of Merom and attacked them.

The LORD gave them into Israel's hands. Israel defeated them and chased them all the way to Greater Sidon, to Misrephoth Maim, and east to the Valley of Mizpah. They struck them down until no survivors were left.
Joshua did to them what the LORD had told him. He cut the leg muscles of their horses and burned their chariots.
Then Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and killed its king with the sword. Hazor had been the leader of all these kingdoms.
They killed everyone in it with the sword and completely destroyed them. Nothing that breathed was left alive, and Joshua burned Hazor.
Joshua captured all these royal cities and their kings. He killed them with the sword and completely destroyed them, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
But Israel did not burn any of the cities built on their mounds, except Hazor, which Joshua burned.
The Israelites kept for themselves all the goods and animals from these cities. But they killed all the people with the sword until they had destroyed them. They left no one alive who breathed.
The LORD had given orders to his servant Moses, and Moses gave them to Joshua, and Joshua obeyed them. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
So Joshua took this whole land: the hill country, the whole Negev, the whole region of Goshen, the western foothills, the Jordan valley, and the hill country of Israel with its foothills,
from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, to Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings and struck them down and put them to death.
Joshua fought against all these kings for a long time.
Not one city made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites living in Gibeon. Israel took all the others in battle.
The LORD himself made their hearts stubborn so that they would fight against Israel. That way they would be completely destroyed without mercy, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua went and wiped out the Anakites from the hill country: from Hebron, Debir and Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and of Israel. Joshua completely destroyed them and their towns.
No Anakites were left in Israel's land. Only in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod did some survive.
So Joshua took the whole land, just as the LORD had told Moses. He gave it to Israel as their own land, divided among their tribes. Then the land had rest from war.
